strengths: Clear problem formulation with well-articulated challenges (interference, redundancy, ambiguity) motivating rank-level decomposition
Novel self-activation mechanism that elegantly uses LoRA key vectors (A) as routers without requiring additional parameters, achieving parameter efficiency (r·din + k·dout)
Comprehensive experimental evaluation across diverse settings: X-TAIL, MTIL, T5/LLaMA2 language models, and code generation with consistent improvements
Thorough ablation studies (Table 4, Fig. 4) validating each component and detailed analysis through visualizations (Figs. 3, 5-6) showing rank specialization and reduced forgetting
Strong parameter efficiency: achieves performance comparable to standard LoRA with ~1/3 activated parameters on HumanEval (26.2M/41.9M)
Rigorous statistical analysis in appendix (Figs. 7-9) demonstrating sparse mixture (only ~10% of ranks needed for 99% activation), supporting core claims
Well-written paper with clear motivation, effective illustrations, and extensive implementation details supporting reproducibility
weaknesses: Modest empirical improvements that may not justify added complexity: X-TAIL Average +1.4% (72.7 vs 71.3%), T5-large +0.9% (77.6 vs 76.7%), with some metrics (Transfer) essentially tied with competitors

Limited theoretical justification for self-activation: the connection between LoRA keys (A_i·x) and relevance is primarily empirical; the claim that load-balancing loss is unnecessary lacks rigorous support

Multiple hyperparameters (τ, δ, k) require task-specific tuning with non-negligible sensitivity; optimal τ varies significantly across models (0.1 vs 0.5) with Fig. 4 showing ~10-20% performance variation—no principled selection guidance provided

Incomplete comparison with MoE-based continual learning methods: focuses on orthogonality-based approaches (O-LoRA, LB-CL) rather than recent MoE variants; limited ablation against MoE-LoRA makes it unclear whether rank-level decomposition is the critical factor
Statistical rigor limited to single run results for most experiments; comprehensive significance testing only in Table 13; modest improvements (1-2%) may not be statistically significant
Misleading 'self-activated' terminology: mechanism still uses temperature scaling and thresholding, indicating external parameter control rather than self-determination
Unclear generalization: X-TAIL Transfer performance essentially tied (63.3% vs CoDyRA 63.2%), limiting claims about improved transfer; MMLU improvements are modest and only tested on single model

strengths: Well-motivated approach addressing concrete limitations of MoE-LoRA through fine-grained rank-level decomposition
Elegant and parameter-efficient self-activation mechanism avoiding external routers (saves ~1.5x parameters)
Comprehensive experimental validation across multiple domains (CLIP, T5, LLaMA2, Llama3.1) with consistent 1-2% improvements and multiple random seeds
Strong practical efficiency: achieves comparable performance to baseline LoRA with only ~1/3 activated parameters
Interpretable rank specialization visualizations (Figs. 3, 5, 6) effectively validating core claims about reduced forgetting and knowledge reuse
Thorough ablation studies (Table 4, Fig. 4) systematically validating each design component
Honest discussion of limitations and good reproducibility with detailed hyperparameters in appendices
weaknesses: Modest improvements (1-2% typically) over strong baselines limits practical significance despite comprehensive evaluation
Insufficient justification for self-activation mechanism—Table 4 shows self-activation matches non-self-activation (60.26% vs 60.09%), undermining its presentation as a key innovation
Linear associative memory theoretical framework (Section 3.2) feels disconnected and takes significant space without rigorously explaining why fine-grained rank selection helps
Multiple hyperparameters (k, τ, δ) requiring task-specific tuning—temperature varies significantly across models (0.1 vs 0.5), adding complexity versus claimed simplicity
Unfair baseline comparisons: MoE-LoRA baseline uses one LoRA per task while MoRA uses r ranks per task; missing comparisons with recent methods like MixLoRA
Lacks analysis of why load-balancing loss is unnecessary, limiting theoretical understanding
Scalability questions unaddressed: only r=4-16 tested; unclear how fine-grained decomposition scales with larger ranks or many sequential tasks (50+)
No statistical significance testing (t-tests, p-values) despite reporting standard deviations
Visualizations (Figs. 3, 5, 6) appear cherry-picked; unclear how common observed rank specialization patterns are across diverse inputs

strengths: Elegant technical formulation using associative memory perspective; self-activation mechanism elegantly eliminates explicit routers without additional parameters

Comprehensive experimental validation across multiple domains (CLIP, LLMs, language classification) with rigorous metrics (Transfer, Average, Last, OP, BWT) and statistical significance reporting (std deviations)
Excellent visualizations demonstrating rank specialization and knowledge reuse; detailed analyses in appendix showing <10% of ranks capture 99% of activation mass
Practical parameter efficiency: achieves comparable/superior performance with ~1/3 the parameters of rank-32 LoRA on CodeAlpaca (41.9M vs 83.9M trainable params)
Thorough ablation studies (Table 4, Figure 4) isolating component contributions; demonstrates contribution of each design choice (sparsity, temperature scaling, thresholding)
Well-presented paper with clear motivation, helpful figures, and comprehensive 30-page appendix including additional experiments and statistical analyses
weaknesses: Modest empirical improvements in many benchmarks: CLIP X-TAIL shows only 1.7% gain over CoDyRA (80.9% vs 79.2%), LLaMA-2-7B shows 1.0% improvement; many gains within noise margins despite extensive tuning

Self-activation superiority claims inadequately supported: Table 4 shows self-activated retrieval (60.26%) underperforms MoE-LoRA baseline (62.56%); improvements come from sparsity constraints and temperature scaling rather than self-activation itself

Multiple ad-hoc design choices: Equation 5 normalization lacks justification; temperature parameter τ highly sensitive and varies dramatically by dataset (0.01 for CLIP, 0.03 for TRACE, 0.5 for CodeAlpaca); activation budget k varies (4-16) without clear selection criteria; introduces three hyperparameters (k, τ, δ) requiring dataset-specific tuning

Insufficient evidence for key claims: 'Experts naturally balanced without regularization' (Section 3.3.4) lacks quantitative load-balance metrics or analysis across diverse domains; claim about balanced experts needs stronger support

Limited theoretical justification: no formal analysis of why rank-1 decomposition fundamentally solves catastrophic forgetting beyond intuition; why rank-1 specifically rather than other granularities not explained

Hyperparameter selection not well-justified: varying k (4-16) and τ by dataset without principled guidance; Figure 4b shows extreme sensitivity to τ (performance swings 60-80%), suggesting method fragility; practitioners unclear how to set hyperparameters for new datasets

Missing computational cost analysis: while Table 18 reports GPU memory, wall-clock times absent; no analysis of how inference cost scales as ranks accumulate; self-activation requires computing scores for all accumulated ranks at every forward pass

Limited novelty in individual components: rank-1 decomposition is straightforward; sparse routing techniques (top-k, temperature, thresholding) are standard MoE methods from prior work ([24], [40], [68]); novel contribution mainly in combination and self-activation
Rank pruning analysis (A.10) is post-hoc: Table 19 shows pruning 30% of parameters with degradation (80.9→79.5%); pruning not integrated into main method, raising questions about design efficiency

Generalization concerns: experiments on relatively standard benchmarks (CLIP, TRACE, standard CL); limited analysis of extreme distribution shifts or adversarial scenarios; performance on diverse unseen domains unclear
